profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the platform integration lead and the workflow/orchestration engineer for a research prototype that adds context-driven self-adaptation to a service-oriented authentication system. The team is preparing the next integration milestone for a demo built on a WComp-like context platform, where authentication behavior changes based on context signals such as location, device trust, and time of day. The agenda is to align on interfaces between the context engine and the authentication workflow, confirm what each side will hand off by the end of the week, and clarify deployment dependencies across environments. The expected outcome is a shared plan for which workflow variant will be wired into the platform, what payload and artifacts will be exchanged, and when the build will be considered ready for QA.

members.name: Nadia Benali
members.expertise: SOA integration, event-driven middleware, context broker services, deployment coordination
members.background: Nadia has been maintaining the service container and context adaptation layer for the lab's ambient computing platform and is responsible for exposing context events to downstream services through stable interfaces.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the integration milestone on schedule without reopening interface discussions, and she is worried that the workflow side may still depend on incomplete sensor connectors that are not reliable enough for the demo.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the system is going to staging, they mean the shared integration cluster with mocked context providers and the current gateway configuration.
The workflow payload naturally includes adaptation metadata like confidence score, risk band, and triggering context snapshot because downstream services need those fields for observability.
If a feature is marked ready for QA, it is acceptable for context events to be injected manually as long as the end-to-end service calls and adaptation branch selection work.
The authentication workflow refers to the default login flow with optional step-up invoked only when the adaptation engine raises a high-risk event.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.expertise: BPMN workflow design, identity flows, service contracts, test automation
members.background: Lucas designs the authentication and authorization workflows that call external identity and policy services, and he recently refactored the case-study flow to support context-aware branching.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid changing the workflow contract again because his branch is already wired to automated tests, and he is concerned that the platform team may deliver environment details too late for his deployment packaging.
hidden_assumptions: When people say staging, they mean the pre-production environment that mirrors production topology, certificates, and external identity endpoints.
The workflow payload means the business request passed between services, not internal adaptation annotations that should stay inside the context engine.
Ready for QA means the workflow can be exercised through live context providers and automated tests without manual event injection or operator intervention.

The authentication workflow refers to the context-aware step-up flow demonstrated in the case study, where extra verification is part of the main coordinated scenario rather than an exceptional branch.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the integration should go to 'staging' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the shared integration cluster used by multiple teams, with mocked context sources and a lighter gateway setup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the pre-production environment that mirrors production certificates, topology, and external identity endpoints.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many teams 'staging' is treated as an ordinary shared term, so each assumes the other is using the local standard definition and sees no reason to unpack it during a short coordination call.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the workflow payload
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Nadia will send Lucas the 'workflow payload' and Lucas will wire it through the authentication services.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the payload includes user/session fields plus adaptation details such as context source, risk band, confidence score, and the triggering event snapshot.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the payload includes only the business fields required by the workflow, while adaptation metadata remains internal to the context platform and is not forwarded through service contracts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They both routinely use 'payload' as shorthand for the data exchanged at the handoff boundary, and the omitted fields feel like implementation detail rather than something worth explicitly listing in a coordination meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they want the integration 'ready for QA' by the end of the week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this is satisfied once the deployment is stable, service calls succeed, and testers can manually inject context events to verify the right branch is chosen.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this is satisfied only when the workflow runs against live context providers and can pass the automated end-to-end QA suite without manual setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are using the same milestone label, the divergence hides inside their internal quality bar; neither expects that a routine status phrase like 'ready for QA' requires calibration.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about connecting 'the authentication workflow' to the context adaptation layer.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the standard login workflow where step-up authentication is an optional branch triggered only for risky contexts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the case-study workflow branch centered on contextual step-up authentication, which he now treats as the main flow for this milestone.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both variants belong to the same feature area and share most services and terminology, so references to 'the authentication workflow' sound perfectly aligned unless someone explicitly names the branch or BPMN file.

If Lucas is still expecting more from the sensor side, I need to keep this focused on what we can actually demo.
